newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-BEAN IN UNCHARTED TERRITORY AGAINST MOORER.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-BEAN IN UNCHARTED TERRITORY AGAINST MOORER.

text.p: Little known Vaughn Bean will be stepping into uncharted territory when he takes on Michael Moorer for the International Boxing Federation heavyweight crown on Saturday.
"He has never been in a fight of this magnitude," Moorer said at a Thursday news conference. "I'm on a totally different level than what he is."
Bean takes a 27-0 record into the fight. But his lack of quality opposition has most calling the fight a mismatch.
The challenger's previous opponents have a dreadful combined record of 126-402-5 and only four had a winning record at the time they fought Bean.
"He hasn't fought the guys that I fought," said the 38-1 Moorer -- an understatement from a man who has had memorable battles with the likes of Evander Holyfield and George Foreman.
In fact, the Nevada Athletic Commission was worried enough about staging an embarrassing mismatch that two members of the commission checked out Bean before approving the fight.
"We did it because there had been some criticism of his record," commission director Marc Ratner said.
Bean is not bothered by the talk of him being in way over his head when he steps into the ring with Moorer.
"It doesn't bother me at all, I got no pressure on me for this fight," said the 23-year-old challenger.
"It's a step up in class, but I prepared myself," said Bean, who will have former champions Joe Frazier and Michael Spinks in his corner.
The Bean camp is counting on their fighter's style to confuse the champion.

"My kid's style, based on what I've seen of Moorer, will give Michael Moorer problems," Bean's promoter Butch Lewis said. "My kid punches well with either hand. Moorer is a guy who does not like what my kid will bringing to him, a lot of pressure."
Lewis is also counting on his record of success with bringing underdog heavyweights to Las Vegas.

"Remember when I came out here with Leon Spinks against Muhammad Ali in 1978 and Michael Spinks against Larry Holmes in 1985. You all know what happened in those fights," he said of the huge upsets by the Spinks brothers.
"Now we are back here with Vaughn. I don't mind being in this seat."
